2: 
3: ## Status And Boundary
4: 
5: This coordinator is the owner-managed, provider-neutral coordination boundary
6: used by the current Gitea mutation path. The coordinator orders and records
7: RelayView effects; provider adapters remain responsible for provider requests,
8: credentials, revision tokens, affected-field comparison, effect proof, and
9: reconciliation. Owner-local serialization is not protection from a human,
10: another owner, or another outside writer.
11: 
12: Planner admission is not a repository singleton: task-scoped planners may submit
13: overlapping work-item effects, and the coordinator—not planner role or
14: project-wide serialization—orders admitted collisions. Tracker read and mutation
15: are explicit separate session admissions; a read-only grant cannot enter this
16: coordinator. The coordinator's sanitized attempts are exposed in API minor 23 and
17: in first-party clients, and provider-free abandonment is visible as a terminal
18: correlated attempt. The deterministic provider-request cost of coordinated
19: mutations, including each phase's preflight and reconciliation reads, is pinned
20: in [Gitea operation cost budgets](gitea-operation-cost-budgets.md).
21: Provider-neutral binding and adapter migration is outside this coordinator.
22: 
23: ## Admission And Queueing
24: 
25: The durable queue key is `(bindingId, targetId, conflictScope)`. The Gitea
26: profile currently maps body edits to `issue_document`, comments to
27: `issue_activity`, labels to `label_membership`, and each dependency mutation to
28: `dependency_edge:<number>`. FIFO is strict within a key; unrelated keys may run
29: concurrently. Each accepted command receives one durable queue ordinal and one
30: effect identity. An exact command retry coalesces with the running promise or
31: returns the existing terminal record and never receives another queue place.
32: 
33: The automatic handoff's owner-managed linked-issue claim is a separate durable
34: owner effect, not an agent-submitted tracker command. It does not receive a
35: planner queue ordinal. Its issue-label preflight, mutation, and readback hold a
36: per-issue gate shared with planner label dispatches in the same owner process.
37: Planner commands retain their FIFO ordering with each other. The claim's
38: persisted state and provider reread govern recovery after owner restart; the
39: gate alone does not prove what happened across a restart or outside the owner.
40: 
41: Queue admission persists actor session/epoch, immutable capability-assignment
42: hash, project/task/binding/target scope, operation, required and available
43: guarantees, opaque basis identity/digest, payload digest, root/predecessor
44: lineage, attempt ordinal, conflict scope, deadline, and lifecycle state. The
45: coordinator revalidates planner/session/project/binding/capability fences at the
46: queue head and again after provider preflight immediately before dispatch.
47: Queue position grants no capability.
48: 
49: The compiled default queue-wait ceiling is 30 seconds and the provider-call
50: deadline is 10 seconds. The provider deadline independently bounds preflight,
51: dispatch, and each reconciliation attempt; all bounds are test-injectable up to five minutes.

53: records `timeout` or `cancelled`, and releases the place. Cancellation requested
54: after dispatch cannot claim absence; the actual provider result or

56: preflight and authorization, immediately before dispatch admission, so cancelling
57: a command during a successful preflight records `cancelled` with zero provider attempts.

1: # Pull-Request Adapter Boundary
2: 
3: ## Current scope
4: 
5: The owner has a version-1 internal, provider-neutral pull-request contract and a
6: Gitea Community implementation. A PR binding is a separate project capability
7: from remote hosting, issue tracking, and CI. Configuration of one does not
8: configure or authorize another. The owner stores at most one enabled PR binding
9: per project as immutable numbered revisions. Replacement and disable require the
10: expected current revision; earlier revisions remain readable for effects that
11: were already admitted. Each binding stores a Gitea instance ID, base URL,
12: repository owner/name and native repository ID, plus a reference to a named
13: systemd credential. The credential value is outside the binding and never
14: appears in API, CLI, or browser projections. The base URL accepts HTTPS or
15: loopback HTTP and rejects embedded credentials, queries, and fragments.
16: 
17: The owner API supports sanitized project-scoped binding list, configure,
18: disable, and probe operations under `/api/v1/settings/pull-requests`. Only the
19: local Unix bearer operator client can configure or disable a binding. The probe
20: authenticates the exact native repository ID and reads the pull-request list;
21: successful read access returns `partial/mutation_unverified`. It does not claim
22: draft creation, review, or merge permission. The `pr list`, `pr configure
23: --file`, `pr disable`, and `pr probe` owner CLI commands use those same routes.
24: Settings displays the sanitized current binding for the selected project. A
25: browser cannot configure or disable it.
26: 
27: An authenticated, project-scoped read at
28: `/api/v1/pull-requests/bindings/:bindingId/pulls/:nativeId` returns a bounded
29: PR observation. `pr inspect` uses that route. It contains the provider/instance/
30: native repository identity, PR number, exact head and base refs and commit
31: revisions, open/closed/merged and draft states, mergeability, supported merge
32: strategy, branch-protection required checks and approval count, advisory commit
33: statuses, attributed review decisions, discussion count, provider update time,
34: and provider URL when it has the configured origin. The Gitea API does not
35: expose a reliable queued-auto-merge read in this contract, so `queuedMerge` is
36: `unknown`; the owner never requests auto-merge. The update time is observation
37: metadata, not a write precondition. A PR with a different native repository ID
38: is rejected even when its owner/name looks similar.
39: 
40: The Gitea adapter reads the repository, PR, base-branch protection, combined
41: head status, and PR reviews. It calls no Issues or Actions route. Reads reject
42: redirects, use a ten-second deadline, and cap each JSON response at one million
43: bytes. Review and status collections are capped at fewer than 100 records; a
44: larger or incomplete collection fails closed. Review identity includes provider
45: review ID, actor ID, login and provider actor type, decision, reviewed head
46: commit, dismissal and staleness flags, and submission time. A comment or
47: reviewer request is not a Human approval. An unknown actor type and a review of
48: another head cannot authorize merge. The latest observed decision per Human
49: actor controls; a later dismissed or stale decision cannot leave an earlier
50: approval effective. Gitea review records carry a reviewed head commit but no
51: review-time base revision. The owner merge authority must bind its Human
52: decision to the current candidate base revision; provider approvals alone are
53: insufficient authority. Required status contexts come from
54: effective branch protection. Other commit statuses remain advisory and their
55: failure does not by itself block merge.
56: 
57: ## Draft effects
58: 
59: The operator-only `POST /api/v1/pull-requests/drafts/:reportId` and `pr draft
60: <report-id>` create a draft only for a confirmed exact hosting publication
61: whose frozen validation policy has a required requirement served exclusively
62: by pull-request CI bindings. The owner resolves the task title, published ref
63: and SHA, PR binding revision, repository identity, and default base branch; the
64: client supplies only the report ID. The hosting publication and PR binding must
65: name the same provider, instance, and native repository. This first-party path
66: does not infer a mapping between different providers. A task whose policy allows
67: a branch-push alternative does not qualify for this command.
68: 
69: Before any create request, the owner stores a draft effect ID with project,
70: task, binding revision, exact head/base refs and head SHA. Gitea draft creation
71: uses a `WIP:` title prefix and verifies the returned PR is actually draft and
72: still points to the exact head. A retry or restart first searches the provider
73: for the same repository and branch pair. A matching draft confirms the retained
74: effect; an uncertain absence remains `unknown` and does not cause a second
75: create. A different head, repository, or base is a conflict. Disabled current
76: bindings do not admit new effects; retained effects resolve through their saved
77: binding revision.
78: 
79: ## Readiness effects
80: 
81: The internal draft-to-ready coordinator requires a trusted owner caller to
82: verify a policy milestone. It stores the binding revision, PR identity, head
83: SHA, base ref and revision, and milestone ID before calling the Gitea title
84: transition. Admission starts in `preflight`; a read or identity failure before
85: dispatch leaves it safely retryable. The owner atomically moves it to `pending`
